events.title: Haymarket Square Riot in Chicago
events.description: During a labor rally in Chicago's Haymarket Square, held in support of workers striking for an eight-hour day, a bomb was thrown at police who were breaking up the gathering. The blast and the gunfire that followed killed several officers and civilians and wounded dozens more.
events.significance: The Haymarket affair and the controversial trials that followed became a global symbol of the labor movement. It is part of the origin of International Workers' Day, observed on May 1 in many countries.

events.title: The United States Begins Building the Panama Canal
events.description: The United States took over the canal project and began construction on the isthmus of Panama. The work followed the failed French effort and meant taking on disease, difficult terrain, and engineering problems on a huge scale.
events.significance: The canal opened in 1914. It cut thousands of miles off sea routes between the Atlantic and Pacific and reshaped global trade and naval strategy.

events.title: Al Capone Begins His Prison Sentence
events.description: Notorious Chicago gangster Al Capone entered the federal penitentiary in Atlanta, Georgia, to begin an eleven-year sentence for tax evasion. Prosecutors had brought him down on financial charges rather than for his violent crimes.
events.significance: His conviction showed that financial investigation could bring down even the most powerful crime bosses. It remains one of the best-known prosecutions in American history.

events.title: Kent State Shootings
events.description: Ohio National Guardsmen opened fire on students protesting the Vietnam War at Kent State University, killing four and wounding nine others.
events.significance: The shootings shocked the nation and deepened opposition to the Vietnam War. They sparked a nationwide student strike and became a lasting emblem of the conflict over the war in America.

events.title: Margaret Thatcher Becomes British Prime Minister
events.description: Following her Conservative Party's election victory, Margaret Thatcher took office as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom. She was the first woman to hold the post.
events.significance: She governed for more than eleven years. Her free-market policies and combative style reshaped British politics and economics, and her legacy is still debated.
